Read and change fields deep inside a nested record of a person, their birth and their address, without writing out every level by hand.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/lens-person) (MIT). Listed under [Collections & Algorithms](/examples/?subject=collections-and-algorithms).

```nomi-run
// FILE: lens_person.nomi
import std/calendar.{self, Date, DateParts}

/// A person: their name, where and when they were born, and where they live.
pub struct Person {
    name: Name
    born: Born
    address: Address
}

/// The fore names and surname of a person.
pub struct Name {
    fore_name: String
    sur_name: String
}

/// Where and on what day someone was born.
pub struct Born {
    at: Address
    on: Date
}

/// A postal address.
pub struct Address {
    house_number: Int
    street: String
    place: String
    country: String
}

/// The street of the address where someone was born.
pub fn born_street(born: Born) -> String {
    born.at.street
}

/// `person` living on `street`, at the same house number and place.
pub fn set_current_street(person: Person, street: String) -> Person {
    #{..person, address: #{.., street}}
}

/// `person` born in `month` of the same year, on the same day, or the
/// calendar's error when that month has no such day.
pub fn set_birth_month(person: Person, month: Int) -> Result<Person, calendar.Error> {
    on = person.born.on
    on = try Date.new(DateParts.year(on), month, DateParts.day(on))

    Ok(#{..person, born: #{.., on}})
}

/// `person` with `rename` applied to the street they were born on and the
/// street they live on.
pub fn rename_streets(person: Person, rename: (String) -> String) -> Person {
    #{
        ..person,
        born: #{.., at: #{.., street: rename(person.born.at.street)}},
        address: #{.., street: rename(person.address.street)},
    }
}

// FILE: lens_person_test.nomi
import {
    std/calendar.Date
    lens_person.{self, Person}
}

once jane = #Person{
    name: #{fore_name: "Jane Joanna", sur_name: "Doe"},
    born: #{
        at: #{
            house_number: 22,
            street: "Implicit Street",
            place: "Lazy Town",
            country: "Haskell Republic",
        },
        on: Date`1970-03-02`,
    },
    address: #{
        house_number: 1337,
        street: "Coder Street",
        place: "Hacker City",
        country: "Functionland",
    },
}

test "bornStreet" {
    assert lens_person.born_street(jane.born) == "Implicit Street"
}

test "setCurrentStreet" {
    moved = lens_person.set_current_street(jane, "Puppy Street")

    assert moved.address.street == "Puppy Street"
    assert moved == #{..jane, address: #{.., street: "Puppy Street"}}
}

test "setBirthMonth" {
    assert Ok(person) = lens_person.set_birth_month(jane, 9)

    assert person.born.on == Date`1970-09-02`
    assert person.born.at == jane.born.at
}

test "renameStreets birth" {
    person = lens_person.rename_streets(jane, String.to_upper)

    assert person.born.at.street == "IMPLICIT STREET"
}

test "renameStreets current" {
    person = lens_person.rename_streets(jane, String.to_upper)

    assert person.address.street == "CODER STREET"
}

// Not canonical: the Haskell track's calendar clips a day past the month's
// end; std/calendar refuses it.
test "a birth month without the birth day is an error" {
    born_on_the_31st = #{..jane, born: #{.., on: Date`1970-03-31`}}

    assert Err(_) = lens_person.set_birth_month(born_on_the_31st, 2)
}
```

## How it's written

- Adapted: the exercise asks for lenses, getter and setter pairs that compose, because in Haskell changing a field three records down means rebuilding each record on the way. Nomi's spread update does that rebuilding itself: `#{..person, address: #{.., street}}` replaces one nested field and keeps the rest, at any depth, and a field path such as `born.at.street` reads one. So the four functions are plain reads and updates, with no `Lens` type; a lens type would be a second spelling of what the update already says.
- The records are four structs, `Person`, `Name`, `Born` and `Address`, with the Haskell track's fields in snake case, and the birth day a std/calendar `Date`.
- `set_birth_month` answers a `Result`: `Date.new` refuses a day the new month does not have, where the Haskell track's `fromGregorian` clips it to the month's last day. The test file adds one case, marked not canonical, that sets February for a person born on the 31st.
- `rename_streets` takes the renaming as a function and applies it to both streets in one update with two nested spreads.
- The exercise has no canonical data. The tests follow the Haskell track's: one person, Jane Joanna Doe, as a `once`, with her birth day written as the checked literal ``Date`1970-03-02` ``, and one test per function. The setters also check that nothing else changed by comparing with a spread update of the original.
